name: cascade_v2 development stream (familiar/unseen alternation)

onset_definition.rule: the first observed interval at which the task's own CPU reaches the registered threshold, given that the previous observed interval was strictly below it; a sustained burst counts once
onset_definition.threshold_basis: strictly above the familiar per-task CPU clip (1860) and below the registered burst floor (4400): only a cascade burst can reach it. Measured offline per-task CPU maximum is 1860 in every auditable corpus, so no familiar task can produce an event.
onset_definition.baseline_free: True.  The registered envelope is admitted at the familiar level and bursts at age 1, so a median-baseline jump has no pre-onset history to compare against (P22-01: max delta_cpu = -4400, zero onsets, while the task really does reach 4400-5200).
onset_definition.response_baseline: median of the task's own pre-onset rows when they exist, else the registered familiar task level; reported per event
onset_definition.source: task's own demand only, never the host aggregate

matched_controls.M0: marginal-matched lag-shuffled: keep every task's marginal amplitude, duration distribution and RAM/Disk windows, but re-pair the windows with a uniformly drawn lag (registered lags destroyed)
matched_controls.M1: order-shuffled: keep the same resource events but reveal them in a randomly permuted temporal order
matched_controls.M2: within-task circular shift: circularly shift each task's RAM/Disk deviation trajectory, preserving marginals and autocorrelation but destroying the registered causal alignment

mechanism.physics_note: controlled unseen temporal resource-demand regime; the two-stage CPU phase is required by Simulator.getPlacementPossible() evaluating demand at the admission interval (P21-01), not a claim about real industrial fault laws

step_semantics: 'steps' is the number of SCORED intervals; the stream arrays carry exactly 'steps' + 1 rows (the trailing guard row feeds the +/-1 label tolerance), the same layout ReplayV3 requires and the pilot streams use

phase_amendment.reason: the workstation cannot host the plan's 3400 intervals: three collection attempts aborted at 1000, 1600 and 2400 intervals with the process at 2.9 GiB and the machine baseline at 12.0 GiB of 15.19 GiB used (problem P22-19).  Segment lengths are scaled by 0.8, preserving the familiar / unseen / familiar / recurrence structure.

bounded_history.note: recovery model is a no-op here and reads only the last window; the tail is 8x the 12-step window the online path uses

ram_guard.amendment: plan 21 registered 3.0 GiB; lowered to 2.5 GiB with explicit user authorisation after the measured growth curve made 3.0 GiB unreachable on this workstation (problem P22-17)
ram_guard.note: a transient dip makes the guard wait, and every wait is recorded here

trim_note: one trailing guard row was removed after collection so the array layout matches the frozen replay contract; no scored interval or registered split window is affected
